speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
theme: When Love Makes the Heart Heavy
hindi: बहुत गहरी करुणा से भरकर, दुखी मन से अर्जुन ने यह कहा: “हे कृष्ण, युद्ध करने की इच्छा से सामने खड़े अपने ही लोगों को देखकर…” (बात अगले श्लोक में पूरी होती है।)
english: Filled with deep compassion and sinking in sorrow, Arjuna spoke these words: “O Krishna, seeing my own family and friends standing here, eager to fight…” His sentence continues in the next verse.
deeper: This verse is like the first drop of rain before a big storm. Arjuna is a great warrior, but when he sees his own people on the battlefield, his heart fills with kṛpā, a soft feeling of pity and care. The word viṣīdan tells us he is not just a little sad. He is sinking, like someone whose feet are slipping in mud.

Notice the words sva-janam, “my own people.” Arjuna does not see enemies. He sees family, teachers and friends. His sorrow grows because he keeps thinking “mine, mine, mine.” Caring for others is beautiful. But when the feeling becomes so heavy that we cannot think clearly, we need wisdom to guide it.

The verse also shows a good habit: Arjuna turns to Krishna and says what he feels, instead of hiding it. He calls out “O Krishna.” Sharing our worries with a wise friend or elder is the first step toward finding the answer. The whole Gita begins from this honest, wobbly moment.
background: Both armies were ready for the great war at Kurukshetra. At Arjuna’s request, Krishna, who was driving his chariot, took it to the middle, between the two armies, so Arjuna could see who stood ready to fight. Krishna said, “Partha, look at all these Kurus gathered here” (1.25).

Arjuna looked and saw grandfathers, teachers, uncles, cousins, sons, friends and well-wishers on both sides (1.26). His heart filled with deep pity and sadness, and he began to speak sorrowfully (1.27). Our verse is where he starts to say what he feels, and the words continue into the next verse.
lessons: Arjuna did not pretend to be fine; it is healthy to notice and name what we feel.
A kind heart that cares about others is one of the best things a person can have.
Too much “mine” can cloud the mind
When we think only of “my people,” sadness can grow so big that we forget what is right to do.
Arjuna told his feelings to Krishna; sharing a worry with a trusted elder or friend is the first step to solving it.
A heavy heart needs time and good guidance before it makes a big decision.
examples: Riya’s best friend Sana is on the opposite team in the school final. Riya suddenly feels funny about trying to win. She learns that she can play fairly and still love her friend.
Aarav finds out that only he or his friend Kabir can get the last scholarship spot. He feels sad and confused about trying his best. He talks to his teacher about it.
Dadaji tells Pooja to stop eating sweets because of his health. She wants to argue, but she sees how worried he looks. Her heart feels heavy, but she understands he is helping her.
Meena sees a thin puppy near her building and her heart fills with pity. She does not just feel sad; she asks her mother how they can help.
Karan and his sister Diya fight over the TV remote. When he sees tears in her eyes, his anger melts into worry. He feels torn between being right and being kind.
Two cousins both want the main part in the school play. Neha is chosen, and she feels sad for her cousin. She hugs her and promises to help her prepare for the next play.
Imran feels a knot in his stomach before the exam, but he hides it for two days. When he finally tells his father, the knot gets smaller. Saying it out loud helped.
Tara sees her cousin copying in a test and feels very torn. She loves him, but she knows honesty matters. She asks her mother how to handle it gently.

story.title: The Kho-Kho Final
paras: Ishaan lived in a small town in Maharashtra. He was the fastest runner on his school’s kho-kho team, and today was the district final. The whole school had come to cheer, and Ishaan was ready.

Then he saw the other team walk in, and his cousin Mihir was in the front, tying his shoes with a big smile. They had grown up together, flying kites and sharing mangoes every summer. Suddenly Ishaan’s legs felt like stone, and he whispered, “How can I try to tag Mihir out?”

His coach saw his face and quietly asked what was wrong. Ishaan told him everything. The coach smiled and said, “Your love for Mihir is good, Ishaan. Playing fair will not take that love away. Think about what is right for the team and the game, and not only about how you feel right now.”

Ishaan took a deep breath. He still felt a little heavy, but now his head was clear. He played honestly, and after the match he hugged Mihir, whichever team had won. That evening, the cousins shared a plate of jalebis.
story.moral: Lesson: A loving heart is a gift, but when feelings get heavy, share them with someone wise and think clearly about what is right.

quiz.q: What filled Arjuna’s heart when he saw his people on the battlefield?
quiz.x: The verse says he was filled with deep kṛpā (compassion) and was sinking in sorrow.
Sva-janam means “my own people,” the relatives and friends Arjuna saw.
Arjuna addressed Krishna, his charioteer and friend, saying “O Krishna.”

quiz.q: What is a good thing to do when your heart feels very heavy?
o: Share it with a wise, trusted person
quiz.x: Arjuna’s example shows that telling a wise friend what we feel is the first step to clarity.

reel.hook: What do you do when your heart feels too heavy to move?
reel.lesson: Caring is beautiful; share heavy feelings with someone wise, then think clearly.
reel.caption:
Arjuna was brave, but even he felt heavy-hearted when he saw his own people. 💔
It is okay to feel, and it is wise to share. Talk to someone you trust today. 🌸
